profile.campus: Data4 MIL01 campus, Cornaredo, Milan (217 MW / 20 ha campus total, distinct from the separate MIL02 site in Vittuone)

source.basis: Operator campus page, structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading: This building, tagged DC06, is one of eight mapped structures on Data4 Italia MIL01 campus at Via Monzoro 101-105 in Cornaredo, a suburb of Milan, Italy. Data4, styled DATA4, is a European data center developer and operator founded in 2006 and headquartered in Paris, France, which its own 2019 published materials describe as controlled by AXA, the French insurance and asset-management group, though the specific AXA entity and any co-investors could not be independently confirmed this session. Data4 own site describes a six-country European footprint spanning France, Italy, Spain, Poland, Germany, and Greece, totaling roughly ten campuses, 1.5 gigawatts of capacity, and 165,000 square meters of IT space group-wide. Data4 has operated in Italy since 2012, developing the Cornaredo campus in progressive phases according to the company own Italian-language press materials. As of an October 2018 company announcement, three data centers were fully operational on the campus with nearly all of that space allocated to customers, and Data4 had banked land for up to seven additional buildings while planning a fourth-generation facility of roughly 2,000 square meters and 3 megawatts of IT power to a Tier 4 design target, formally inaugurated at a June 2019 campus event. The DC06 numbering suggests this building represents a later expansion phase beyond that fourth-generation facility, though the exact construction or opening date for DC06 specifically could not be confirmed. Data4 current Milan-area location page describes the Cornaredo site, referred to as MIL01, as a 217 megawatt, 20 hectare campus, distinct from a separate second Milan-area site in Vittuone known as MIL02. No Data4 source reviewed breaks the 217 megawatt campus figure down by individual building, so no capacity or square footage figure specific to DC06 alone is asserted here, and no tenant is named.
profile.capacity_note: Campus level total published, 170 MW and 20 hectares, not broken down per building, so no per building MW or square footage figure is recorded.
profile.research_note: Campus-level 217 MW / 20 ha figure from Data4 own Milan location page, explicitly not assigned to this individual building. DC06 numbering places it after the land-banked expansion phase, exact date unconfirmed. DC vs DCL naming distinction not explained by any Data4 source.

reading.body:
Data4's MIL01 campus near Milan operates at 170 MW total electrical capacity across 20 hectares, but the operator publishes power and footprint only at the campus level, not per building, leaving individual facility capacity unknown.

Data4 operates the MIL01 campus as eight separate buildings, each catalogued in registries with its own identifier. DC06 is one of these buildings. Because Data4 discloses capacity as a single campus figure rather than per facility, the electrical draw and physical size of DC06 cannot be isolated from the total. This practice is common among multi-building operators. It obscures the scaling pattern that matters for power constraint analysis: whether a single source can sustain growth across all eight facilities, and whether any one building approaches the infrastructure limits of its location.

The data confirms Data4 Italia's address and parent company, headquartered in Paris and operating across six European countries. It does not reveal whether Data4 or other operators control available power supply to this campus, nor whether the 170 MW figure represents installed capacity, peak draw, or planned expansion. Without per-building figures or grid connection details, the campus total conveys scale but not the distribution of load or constraint within Cornaredo.
